thread:
lina: Heads-up: flaky test failures in CI when running our sample-app tests with Vitest + ESM. Locally green, GH actions show random import/mocking errors. Repro steps attached. Anyone seen this with edge runtime?
josh: Seen similar. What error message are you getting?
lina: Two variants: one run shows `TypeError: (0 , _inference.createClient) is not a function` and another shows `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` when jest tries to run the same file. Very confusing.
priya: Classic ESM/CJS interop problem. Are you importing default or named? And what's in package.json exports?
lina: Codebase uses `import inference from '@redwood/inference'` (default). SDK currently ships an ESM bundle (dist/index.mjs) and we added a tiny dist/index.cjs shim but exports map is minimal. package.json has "type":"module" at sample-app level.
josh: Vitest sometimes pre-bundles deps which changes the module shape. Try adding this to vitest config: `test: { deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference'] } }` so vite doesn't rewrite the package. Also set `resolve: { conditions: ['import', 'worker'] }` for edge.
priya: For jest, if it tries to `require()` an ESM-only package you get ERR_REQUIRE_ESM. Fixes: publish dual cjs/esm and add `exports` map with both import/require entries, or add a small cjs file and point `require` to it in exports.
lina: I tried changing tests to `import * as inference from '@redwood/inference'` which reduced flakes locally but CI still had runs failing.
josh: When mocking, ensure mock preserves module shape. Instead of `vi.mock('@redwood/inference', () => ({ createClient: () => ... }))`, do `vi.mock('@redwood/inference', async () => { const actual = await vi.importActual('@redwood/inference'); return { __esModule: true, ...actual, createClient: () => ({ predict: () => 'ok' }) } })`. That keeps default/named resolution consistent.
priya: Add a test types shim so TS in the runner doesn't complain: create `test/types.d.ts` with `declare module '@redwood/inference' { export function createClient(...args:any): any; export default any; }` and reference it in tsconfig.test.json's `include` or `typeRoots`.
nina: (typo) lina: Good call. Also worth checking Vitest's `transformMode.web` and `esbuild.target` to match the published bundle target. I added `transformMode: { web: [/\.ts$/] }, esbuild: { target: 'es2020' }` and it helped in GH actions.
josh: CI difference often comes down to node version in GH actions runner vs local. Make sure matrix tests include node 18/20 and use the same yarn/pnpm flags.
priya: Filed minimal repro + logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/531 — includes sample project with type:module, vitest config, and failing GH action.
ci-bot: Issue created (#531) and linked to repository redwood-inference/sdk-js.
docs-bot: Suggest adding Troubleshooting note in sample-app README covering: 1) vitest snippet (`deps.inline` + `environment: 'edge-runtime'` + `resolve.conditions`), 2) mocking pattern that preserves `__esModule`, and 3) TS shim for tests. Would you like me to open a docs PR?
lina: Yes please add the docs PR referencing issue #531. Short-term workaround: change tests to named imports + inline deps in vitest. Long-term: SDK should publish a canonical exports map + bundled d.ts and a small CJS shim.
josh: I'll draft the SDK PR to update package.json exports and include dist/index.cjs + index.mjs + index.d.ts. Priya, can you validate the repro once I push?
priya: Yep, will run matrix on GH actions. Marking thread resolved for devex but keeping issue open until SDK release lands. :+1:
